newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 higher Wednesday in a technical correction to the market's two-day decline, traders said.

A weaker dollar against Sterling should also bolster the market, they said. Sterling jumped after a larger-than-expected 59,400 drop in UK April unemployment. That was against forecasts for a 40,000 decline.

New York cocoa futures ended sharply lower in light dealings Tuesday, pressured by a late-session round of speculative liquidation. July settled down $20 a at $1,409 a tonne after trading from $1,422 to 1,404. September shed $18 to $1,439, with the rest down $15 to $29.
Technically, traders pegged July resistance at $1,420 to $1,422, with near-term support at $1,400. A major downside objective was noted at $1,385.

London cocoa futures were barely changed in thin, directionless dealings early Wednesday. At the midday break, LIFFE July cocoa was down two stg at 998 stg, while September was up one stg at 1,018. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
